features.foot: Click-to-focus support depends on your terminal and OS. OpenCode: silent completion, question, permission and error alerts for root sessions. No sound or click-to-focus.

terminalSupport.intro: Claude Code and Codex CLI only. Click-to-focus adapts to what you already run. Here is exactly how precise the click gets on each platform.
terminalSupport.legend: Exact tab/pane focuses the precise split or tab. Window-level raises the whole app window. Best-effort means the plugin tries a generic match that may land on the wrong window.
terminalSupport.windowsNote: On Windows, focus is always window-level — there is no public API to target one tab inside Windows Terminal.
terminalSupport.fallbackNote: Any other terminal still works through generic window matching. Override the detected app with a custom bundle ID on macOS.

notes.ghosttyAutomation: Needs Automation permission for exact tab focus.
notes.ghosttyUnverified: Mapped in the Linux daemon but not yet officially verified.
notes.itermPythonApi: Requires enabling iTerm2's Python API, then a restart.
notes.warpDeepLink: No extra permissions needed — Warp resolves its own window, tab, and pane.
notes.kittyRemoteControl: Exact pane targeting needs kitty's remote control enabled.
notes.wezPane: Targets the exact pane through WezTerm's own CLI.
notes.jetbrainsGeneric: macOS detects it the same way as any other app, not with a dedicated integration.
notes.jetbrainsLinuxDetect: Linux detects the IDE via its process tree and product-info.json window class. The terminal tab inside it isn't selectable.
notes.genericFallback: Falls back to generic window matching, not a dedicated integration.
notes.appleTerminalFallback: Also the default fallback when no other terminal is detected.
notes.terminatorTitle: Uses the exact window title for precise matching.
notes.tmuxItermCC: Also works inside iTerm2's -CC control mode.
notes.zellijLinuxPane: Linux targets the exact pane when the session exports it, otherwise falls back to the active tab by name.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to get back to work.

1.question: Do I need every agent installed?
1.answer: Select any combination of Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode. Install the selected agents first; the commands below install notifications.

2.question: Are Codex hooks installed automatically?
2.answer: Yes. The installer registers the hooks and saves a stable runtime copy. Open /hooks in Codex to review and trust them. Changed definitions need review again.

3.question: Will an update reset my settings?
3.answer: The installer preserves your shared configuration and foreign Codex hooks. Install and update use the same command. Restart the selected agent after updating.

4.question: Can I choose what makes a sound?
4.answer: Yes. Configure sounds, volume, audio device and notification channels. Choose Configure in the guide for the steps specific to your agent. Claude Code and Codex CLI only.

5.question: Does click-to-focus work everywhere?
5.answer: Support varies by OS and terminal. iTerm2 needs its Python API for precise tab targeting. Windows focuses a window, not an exact tab. OpenCode: silent completion, question, permission and error alerts for root sessions. No sound or click-to-focus.

6.question: What if I don't get a notification?
6.answer: Check your OS notification permissions and chosen channels. For Codex, confirm the hooks are trusted.

capabilities.title: Selected agent capabilities
capabilities.claude: Completion, review, question, plan, session limit and API error alerts, with sounds and click-to-focus where supported.
capabilities.codex: Completion and permission alerts, with sounds and click-to-focus where supported. Review and trust installed hooks in /hooks.
capabilities.opencode: Silent completion, question, permission and error alerts for root sessions. No sound or click-to-focus.

opencode.channelsHint: These choices apply only to OpenCode. Allow at least one channel; webhook URLs are configured separately.
opencode.scope: OpenCode: silent completion, question, permission and error alerts for root sessions. No sound or click-to-focus.
opencode.version: Tested with OpenCode 1.18.33. Requires plugin release 1.46.0 or newer. OpenCode V2 is not supported.
opencode.chooseChannel: Choose at least one notification channel.
opencode.restart: Restart OpenCode to load the global plugin. On macOS, grant notification permission using the setup guide.
opencode.configure: Use config path for shared settings. Enable desktop/webhook consent with setup-opencode; configure webhook endpoints separately.
